title: NorCal to SoCal A Guide to Californian Slang
paragraphs: California is a big state, and people in different parts of it sometimes use different words. Here is a short guide to some slang from Northern California, or NorCal, and Southern California, or SoCal.

The most famous NorCal word is "hella." It means "very" or "a lot." For example, you might hear someone say, "That movie was hella good." The word started in the San Francisco Bay Area. Today, people in other parts of California may also use it, but some people in SoCal do not like it.
In NorCal, "the City" means San Francisco. Another NorCal word is "hyphy." It was first the name of a style of rap music from the Bay Area, but now it also describes something wild or full of energy.
In SoCal, much slang comes from surf culture. "Gnarly" means amazing or impressive. "Stoked" means very excited, and "dude" is a friendly word for a person.

There is also a famous difference in how people talk about highways. In SoCal, people put the word "the" before highway numbers, so they say "the 101" or "the 5." In NorCal, people usually just say "101" or "5."
Finally, the names "NorCal" and "SoCal" are used more by people in Northern California. People in Southern California do not often call their area "SoCal."
Learning these words can help visitors to the state understand Californians a little better.
